product_family: Stripe AI comprises AI-powered payment optimization features integrated into Stripe's core platform, including personalized checkout, fraud detection (Radar), revenue recovery (Smart Retries), payment intelligence, and the Stripe Payments Foundation Model (a self-supervised foundation model trained on tens of billions of transactions that distills each payment into an embedding; described by Stripe as a foundation model, not a large language model). Includes specialized products: Agentic Commerce Suite, Machine Payments Protocol, and Link digital wallet for AI agents.

certifications.name: ISO 27001
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence found on Stripe's own domain of an ISO 27001 certification. Stripe's security page (docs.stripe.com/security) enumerates PCI Level 1, SOC 1/2/3, PA-DSS, EMVCo, NIST CSF, CBPR, PRP, and the Data Privacy Frameworks, but does not list ISO 27001. (Stripe requires ISO 27001 of its own suppliers, which is not the same as Stripe holding it.)

Stripe can be used in payment workflows only when no Protected Health Information (PHI) is transmitted or stored through it. Treat as unsuitable for PHI use cases absent a BAA.

privacy.ai_training_note: Stripe's Payments Foundation Model trains on billions of historical transactions to optimize payment processing. Training data includes: authorization/decline history (cards, customers, merchants), transaction features (merchant, amount, decline reason), and card features (BIN, issuer, expiry). US customers have right to opt out of sale/sharing of personal information. Merchants must disclose data sharing with Stripe to their end customers per the Data Processing Agreement.
privacy.data_region: Multiple regions with regional compliance (EU, UK, US, Swiss frameworks supported)

products.name: Stripe Payments
products.data_scope: Card data (tokenized), transaction amounts, merchant data, authorization/decline history
products.notes: Core payment processing with PCI DSS Level 1 compliance. Stripe tokenizes card data to avoid PCI scope for merchants.

products.name: Stripe AI / Payments Intelligence Suite
products.data_scope: Historical transaction patterns, customer behavior, fraud signals, authorization trends
products.notes: Trained on billions of transactions. Includes Radar (fraud detection), Smart Retries (revenue recovery ~57% of failed recurring payments), personalized checkout (11.9% revenue increase avg), and Authorization Boost (2.2% approval rate increase).

products.name: Agentic Commerce Suite
products.data_scope: Purchase data, product catalog, customer intent signals
products.notes: Enables businesses to sell inside AI apps and agents. Partnership with Google for sales in Gemini and AI Mode. Announced at Sessions 2026.

products.name: Link Digital Wallet for Agents
products.data_scope: Payment credentials, transaction history, agent authorization tokens
products.notes: 250M+ global users. Enables autonomous AI agents to make payments on behalf of users.

products.name: Machine Payments Protocol
products.data_scope: Microtransaction data, recurring payment instructions, stablecoin/fiat settlement data
products.notes: Real-time payments streaming for AI-native business models. Includes programmatic microtransactions and stablecoin/fiat settlement.

products.name: Stripe Payments Foundation Model
products.data_scope: Aggregated payment patterns, authorization/decline signals, merchant-customer-card relationships (anonymized at inference)
products.notes: Self-supervised foundation model trained on tens of billions of transactions, distilling each payment into a versatile embedding. Stripe describes it as a payments foundation model (not a large language model). Used across Radar, Smart Retries, and other AI products.

compare.pricing_model: Usage-based (per transaction) with fixed + variable fee structure. Varies by product (Payments, Radar, Billing, etc.). No minimum.
compare.data_residency: Multi-region with regional compliance frameworks (EU, UK, US). Data processing per DPA specifies controller/processor roles. Supports EU-US DPF, UK-US DPF, Swiss-US DPF for transatlantic transfers.

flags: 'stripe-ai' refers to Stripe's AI-powered payment features (e.g., Payments Foundation Model, Radar, Smart Retries), not a standalone AI product. Stripe is fundamentally a payment/fintech company with enterprise maturity, not an AI tool vendor in the traditional sense.

Stripe's Payments Foundation Model trains on customer transaction data at scale (billions of transactions). US customers have opt-out rights per the Privacy Act; EU customers should confirm their rights under GDPR. Merchants must disclose data usage to end customers.
Stripe does not offer a HIPAA BAA and is not suitable for healthcare/PHI use cases without additional safeguards. This is a hard boundary.
No FedRAMP authorization. If federal government compliance is required, Stripe is not suitable.

No public evidence was found on Stripe's own domain of ISO 27001, ISO 27017 (cloud security), or ISO 27018 (cloud PII) certifications. Stripe's security page relies on PCI Level 1, SOC 1/2/3, and the Data Privacy Frameworks instead.

Stripe has not published an ISO 42001 (AI governance) certification despite shipping a large-scale foundation model. This may indicate no formal AI governance framework audit, or that one is unannounced.
trust.stripe.com exists but is partially JavaScript-rendered and requires an NDA for SOC reports; not as transparent as some competitors' trust centers.
